====== Start a business in Illinois (LLC filing path) ======

**Illinois · How do I start a business?** · state model checked by Claude · quality 1.00

//Generated by [[https://github.com/alibama/lexflow|lexflow]] from the state statutes (open-us-law, government publisher text) and checked by Claude: every quoted phrase was matched word for word against the statute text, and the process passed the BPMN/DMN schemas, bpmnlint and a Petri-net soundness check. Information, not legal advice.//

**Governing law:** [[https://www.ilga.gov/ftp/ILCS/Ch%200805/Act%200180/080501800K5-1.html|805 ILCS 180/5-1]] — Section 5-1

  <bpmn:collaboration id="collab_il_business" name="Start a business in Illinois (LLC filing path)">
    <bpmn:documentation textFormat="text/plain">Someone wants to start a business, here as a limited liability company</bpmn:documentation>
    <bpmn:extensionElements>
      <lex:model id="il-business" jurisdiction="il" jurisdictionName="Illinois" reviewStatus="draft" method="gold-manual">
        <lex:gap>Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step (articles of organization under 805 ILCS 180/5-1, 5-5 and 5-55). Illinois issues no separate certificate of organization: the Secretary of State endorses "Filed" and the date and files the original (§ 5-55(a)(3)(A), (B)), and the company is organized when the articles are filed or on a later date specified in them (§ 5-5(b)). The other structures are not modelled step by step: a limited partnership is formed when the Secretary of State files its certificate (805 ILCS 215/201(c)); a partnership becomes an LLP by filing a statement of qualification, and the Secretary of State must register any partnership that submits a completed application with the required fee (805 ILCS 206/1001(c), (i)).</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Filing evidence for the articles is the Secretary of State's filing itself (§ 5-5(b)), not necessarily a returned copy. Under § 5-55(a)(1) a copy is delivered only when the Act requires the document to be filed in duplicate; the LLC Act requires duplicates for an assumed name application (§ 1-20(b)) but not for articles of organization (§§ 5-5 and 5-45 are silent). So the endorse-and-return-the-copy duty (§ 5-55(a)(3)(A), (C)) is modelled only on the assumed name branch; if a filer does deliver a copy of the articles, the endorsement on "the copy" and its return would apply there too.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The delayed effective date in § 5-5(b) (any later time specified in the articles, not more than 60 days after filing) is a ceiling on the date the articles may choose, not a period for anyone to act, and nothing happens when it runs; it is therefore not drawn as a timer. The outcome llc_exists follows the filing; with a delayed date the company is organized on the specified date instead.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The Secretary of State's review is modelled from the contents list in § 5-5(a), organizer eligibility under § 5-1(a) and the fee rule in § 5-55(a). The name requirements of § 1-10, the duration clause (§ 5-5(a)(5.5), perpetual unless stated) and the signing rules of § 5-45 are not checked here.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Interrogatories (§ 5-60): the Secretary of State may send them; they must be answered in writing and under oath within 30 days after mailing or any additional time the Secretary fixes (the extension is not modelled), and the document need not be filed until they are answered, and not then if the answers show non-conformity (that second limb is covered by the review decision). Failing to answer in time is also a petty offense (§ 1-20(h)). § 5-60 directs interrogatories to the company's managers or members; how they reach an organizer before the company exists is not stated, so the company is shown as the answering party. The missed-deadline consequence is recorded as 'unstated' because the text says only that the Secretary need not file, not that the filing is refused or deemed denied.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The statute sets no time limit for the Secretary of State to act on the articles, and says nothing about what happens to non-conforming articles beyond not filing them; rejection and resubmission are not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Trust-company LLCs need a statement from the Secretary of Financial and Professional Regulation before filing, and bank or savings-bank LLCs file with that Department or a federal regulator instead (§ 5-5(c), (d)); not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>An LLC that trades under an assumed name files in duplicate with the Secretary of State under § 1-20, not with the County Clerk (805 ILCS 405/4). The assumed-name fee is prorated by the year in the five-year cycle (§ 50-10(b)(9)); the right runs from the Secretary's filing date (§ 1-20(c)). Renewal every five years with the annual report (§ 1-20(c), (d)) is not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Sole proprietors and general partnerships using an assumed name file with the County Clerk of every county where they do business, publish notice for 3 consecutive weeks starting within 15 days, and file proof of publication within 50 days or the registration is void (805 ILCS 405/1); trading without complying is a Class C misdemeanor, each day a separate offence (805 ILCS 405/5, not cited in sections). The county's filing fee is not stated in the Act.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>State formation is only part of starting a business: Illinois has no single statewide general business licence. Municipal and county licences, state tax registration (Illinois Department of Revenue) and occupational licences come from other laws and local ordinances, which are scored separately.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Professionals: a professional corporation needs every organizer licensed for the same or related professional services (805 ILCS 10/6) and a certificate of registration from the regulating authority before opening an establishment ($50, 805 ILCS 10/12(a)); a professional LLC files articles stating the professional service (805 ILCS 185/11) and needs a Department certificate of registration before opening an establishment ($50, 805 ILCS 185/15(b), (c)). A separate registration application is needed for each business location (805 ILCS 185/15(d)), and registrations expire every third January 1 with a $40 renewal (805 ILCS 185/15(e)); these are not modelled as steps. Licensed persons may still use other permitted business forms (805 ILCS 10/4, not cited in sections).</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>LLP as a liability shield: the structure table keeps the seven-rule order shared with other states, so a multi-owner business wanting limited liability is routed to the LLC rule, which names the LLP (805 ILCS 206/1001) as an alternative; the general-partnership rule names it as an optional later step.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Business corporations owe an initial franchise tax under the Business Corporation Act in addition to the $150 filing fee; the tax sections are not printed here.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The 'required fee' for an LLP statement of qualification is not stated in the sections printed (805 ILCS 206/1001(e)); LLP status lasts one year after filing, so renewal is presupposed but not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Not-for-profit corporation status is a state corporate form, not tax exemption; federal 501(c) status is outside the Illinois Compiled Statutes and not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Annual reports ($75 for an LLC, § 50-10(b)(11); $75 for a business corporation, 805 ILCS 5/15.10(o); $10 for a not-for-profit, 805 ILCS 105/115.10(m); $100 for a limited partnership, 805 ILCS 215/1302(b)(6)) are not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>LLCs with series or the ability to establish a series pay $400 instead of $150 (§ 50-10(b)(1)); not modelled in the fee step.</lex:gap>

===== Steps and the words they come from =====

  - **Execute and deliver articles of organization** — Organizer (founder) · //permission// (§ 5-1(a)) \\ “//may organize a limited liability company by executing and delivering articles of organization to the Secretary of State as specified in Sections 5-5 and 5-45//”
  - **Collect the $150 filing fee** — Secretary of State · //obligation// (§ 50-10(b)(1)) \\ “//Filing articles of organization (domestic), application for admission (foreign), and restated articles of organization (domestic), $150.//”
  - **Send interrogatories on compliance** — Secretary of State · //permission// (§ 5-60) \\ “//The Secretary of State may propound to any limited liability company or foreign limited liability company subject to the provisions of this Act//”
  - **Answer interrogatories in writing under oath** — Limited liability company (its managers or, if none, its members) · within 30 days · //obligation// (§ 5-60) \\ “//the answers thereto shall be full and complete and shall be made in writing and under oath//”
  - **Check articles conform and fees paid** — Secretary of State · //obligation// (§ 5-55(a)(3)) \\ “//unless the Secretary of State finds that the document does not conform to law, he or she shall, when all fees have been paid//”
  - **Endorse "Filed" and the filing date** — Secretary of State · //obligation// (§ 5-55(a)(3)(A)) \\ “//endorse on the original and on the copy the word "Filed" and the month, day, and year of the filing thereof//”
  - **File the original articles** — Secretary of State · //obligation// (§ 5-55(a)(3)(B)) \\ “//file in his or her office the original of the document//”
  - **File assumed name application in duplicate** — Limited liability company (its managers or, if none, its members) · //obligation// (§ 1-20(b)) \\ “//Before transacting any business in Illinois under an assumed limited liability company name or names, the limited liability company shall, for each assumed name, execute and file in duplicate an application//”
  - **Collect the prorated assumed name fee** — Secretary of State · //obligation// (§ 50-10(b)(9)) \\ “//Filing an application for use of an assumed name under Section 1-20 of this Act, $150 for each year or part thereof ending in 0 or 5//”
  - **Endorse and file the assumed name application** — Secretary of State · //obligation// (§ 5-55(a)(3)(B)) \\ “//file in his or her office the original of the document//”
  - **Return the filed duplicate to the company** — Secretary of State · //obligation// (§ 5-55(a)(3)%%(C)%%) \\ “//return the copy to the person who filed it or to that person's representative//”

===== Which business structure fits, and what must be filed with the state? =====

Decision table (DMN), hit policy FIRST.

^ Organized for a nonprofit or charitable purpose ^ Owners render a licensed professional service ^ Number of owners ^ Owners want protection from the business's debts ^ Plans to sell shares to outside investors ^ Some co-owners will be passive investors only ^ → Business structure ^ → What is filed, and where ^ → State filing fee ^ Source ^
| true | - | - | - | - | - | Not-for-profit corporation (General Not For Profit Corporation Act of 1986) | Articles of incorporation, filed with the Secretary of State | $50 for filing articles of incorporation (805 ILCS 105/115.10(a)) | § 102.05 |
| false | true | - | true | - | - | Professional corporation (Professional Service Corporation Act, 805 ILCS 10) or professional limited liability company (Professional Limited Liability Company Act, 805 ILCS 185; an LLC providing a professional service licensed by the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation must be formed under that Act, 805 ILCS 180/1-25(d)); each organizer of a professional corporation must be licensed in Illinois to perform the same professional service or related professional services (805 ILCS 10/6) | Articles of incorporation (professional corporation) or articles of organization (professional LLC, 805 ILCS 185/11), filed with the Secretary of State on the Secretary's forms and stating the specific profession; before opening an establishment, a professional corporation needs a certificate of registration from the regulating authority (805 ILCS 10/12(a)) and a professional LLC needs a certificate of registration from the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (805 ILCS 185/15(b)) | Professional corporation: $150 for articles of incorporation (805 ILCS 5/15.10(a)) plus initial franchise tax under the Business Corporation Act, and a $50 certificate of registration (805 ILCS 10/12(a)); professional LLC: $150 (805 ILCS 180/50-10(b)(1)) + $50 certificate of registration (805 ILCS 185/15%%(c)%%) | § 6 |
| false | - | - | true | true | - | Business corporation (Business Corporation Act of 1983) | Articles of incorporation, executed and filed in duplicate with the Secretary of State (805 ILCS 5/2.10) | $150 for filing articles of incorporation (805 ILCS 5/15.10(a)), plus initial franchise tax under the Business Corporation Act (not printed here) | § 2.05(a) |
| false | - | %%>%%= 2 | true | - | true | Limited partnership (limited partners are shielded; all general partners are liable jointly and severally for the partnership's obligations, 805 ILCS 215/404(a), except for obligations incurred while it is a limited liability limited partnership, 805 ILCS 215/404%%(c)%%; the certificate must state whether it is one, 805 ILCS 215/201(a)(4)) | Certificate of limited partnership, delivered to the Secretary of State for filing | $150 (805 ILCS 215/1302(b)(1)) | § 201(a) |
| false | - | - | true | - | - | Limited liability company (with 2 or more owners, an alternative shield is a general partnership registered as a limited liability partnership by filing a statement of qualification, 805 ILCS 206/1001(a), %%(c)%%) | Articles of organization, executed and delivered to the Secretary of State | $150; $400 for a company with series (805 ILCS 180/50-10(b)(1)) | § 5-1(a) |
| false | - | 1 | false | - | - | Sole proprietorship | No formation filing; before trading under any name other than the owner's real name, file an assumed name certificate with the County Clerk of each county where the business is conducted, publish notice of the filing once a week for 3 consecutive weeks (first within 15 days), and file proof of publication with the County Clerk within 50 days, or the registration is void (805 ILCS 405/1) | None to form; the County Clerk's filing fee and the newspaper's publication charge for an assumed name are not set in 805 ILCS 405/1 | § 1 |
| false | - | %%>%%= 2 | false | - | - | General partnership | No formation filing: 2 or more co-owners carrying on a business for profit form a partnership. A partnership trading under a name that does not include its partners' real names must file an assumed name certificate with the County Clerk and publish notice (805 ILCS 405/1, 405/4). Optionally, after approval by the vote needed to amend the partnership agreement, the partnership may file a statement of qualification with the Secretary of State to become a limited liability partnership; the status remains effective for one year after filing (805 ILCS 206/1001(b), %%(c)%%, (e)) | None to form; County Clerk fee and publication charge for an assumed name; the 'required fee' for an LLP statement of qualification (805 ILCS 206/1001(e)) is set outside the sections printed here | § 202(a) |

===== What the text leaves open =====

  * Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step (articles of organization under 805 ILCS 180/5-1, 5-5 and 5-55). Illinois issues no separate certificate of organization: the Secretary of State endorses "Filed" and the date and files the original (§ 5-55(a)(3)(A), (B)), and the company is organized when the articles are filed or on a later date specified in them (§ 5-5(b)). The other structures are not modelled step by step: a limited partnership is formed when the Secretary of State files its certificate (805 ILCS 215/201%%(c)%%); a partnership becomes an LLP by filing a statement of qualification, and the Secretary of State must register any partnership that submits a completed application with the required fee (805 ILCS 206/1001%%(c)%%, (i)).
  * Filing evidence for the articles is the Secretary of State's filing itself (§ 5-5(b)), not necessarily a returned copy. Under § 5-55(a)(1) a copy is delivered only when the Act requires the document to be filed in duplicate; the LLC Act requires duplicates for an assumed name application (§ 1-20(b)) but not for articles of organization (§§ 5-5 and 5-45 are silent). So the endorse-and-return-the-copy duty (§ 5-55(a)(3)(A), %%(C)%%) is modelled only on the assumed name branch; if a filer does deliver a copy of the articles, the endorsement on "the copy" and its return would apply there too.
  * The delayed effective date in § 5-5(b) (any later time specified in the articles, not more than 60 days after filing) is a ceiling on the date the articles may choose, not a period for anyone to act, and nothing happens when it runs; it is therefore not drawn as a timer. The outcome llc_exists follows the filing; with a delayed date the company is organized on the specified date instead.
  * The Secretary of State's review is modelled from the contents list in § 5-5(a), organizer eligibility under § 5-1(a) and the fee rule in § 5-55(a). The name requirements of § 1-10, the duration clause (§ 5-5(a)(5.5), perpetual unless stated) and the signing rules of § 5-45 are not checked here.
  * Interrogatories (§ 5-60): the Secretary of State may send them; they must be answered in writing and under oath within 30 days after mailing or any additional time the Secretary fixes (the extension is not modelled), and the document need not be filed until they are answered, and not then if the answers show non-conformity (that second limb is covered by the review decision). Failing to answer in time is also a petty offense (§ 1-20(h)). § 5-60 directs interrogatories to the company's managers or members; how they reach an organizer before the company exists is not stated, so the company is shown as the answering party. The missed-deadline consequence is recorded as 'unstated' because the text says only that the Secretary need not file, not that the filing is refused or deemed denied.
  * The statute sets no time limit for the Secretary of State to act on the articles, and says nothing about what happens to non-conforming articles beyond not filing them; rejection and resubmission are not modelled.
  * Trust-company LLCs need a statement from the Secretary of Financial and Professional Regulation before filing, and bank or savings-bank LLCs file with that Department or a federal regulator instead (§ 5-5%%(c)%%, (d)); not modelled.
  * An LLC that trades under an assumed name files in duplicate with the Secretary of State under § 1-20, not with the County Clerk (805 ILCS 405/4). The assumed-name fee is prorated by the year in the five-year cycle (§ 50-10(b)(9)); the right runs from the Secretary's filing date (§ 1-20%%(c)%%). Renewal every five years with the annual report (§ 1-20%%(c)%%, (d)) is not modelled.
  * Sole proprietors and general partnerships using an assumed name file with the County Clerk of every county where they do business, publish notice for 3 consecutive weeks starting within 15 days, and file proof of publication within 50 days or the registration is void (805 ILCS 405/1); trading without complying is a Class C misdemeanor, each day a separate offence (805 ILCS 405/5, not cited in sections). The county's filing fee is not stated in the Act.
  * State formation is only part of starting a business: Illinois has no single statewide general business licence. Municipal and county licences, state tax registration (Illinois Department of Revenue) and occupational licences come from other laws and local ordinances, which are scored separately.
  * Professionals: a professional corporation needs every organizer licensed for the same or related professional services (805 ILCS 10/6) and a certificate of registration from the regulating authority before opening an establishment ($50, 805 ILCS 10/12(a)); a professional LLC files articles stating the professional service (805 ILCS 185/11) and needs a Department certificate of registration before opening an establishment ($50, 805 ILCS 185/15(b), %%(c)%%). A separate registration application is needed for each business location (805 ILCS 185/15(d)), and registrations expire every third January 1 with a $40 renewal (805 ILCS 185/15(e)); these are not modelled as steps. Licensed persons may still use other permitted business forms (805 ILCS 10/4, not cited in sections).
  * LLP as a liability shield: the structure table keeps the seven-rule order shared with other states, so a multi-owner business wanting limited liability is routed to the LLC rule, which names the LLP (805 ILCS 206/1001) as an alternative; the general-partnership rule names it as an optional later step.
  * Business corporations owe an initial franchise tax under the Business Corporation Act in addition to the $150 filing fee; the tax sections are not printed here.
  * The 'required fee' for an LLP statement of qualification is not stated in the sections printed (805 ILCS 206/1001(e)); LLP status lasts one year after filing, so renewal is presupposed but not modelled.
  * Not-for-profit corporation status is a state corporate form, not tax exemption; federal 501%%(c)%% status is outside the Illinois Compiled Statutes and not modelled.
  * Annual reports ($75 for an LLC, § 50-10(b)(11); $75 for a business corporation, 805 ILCS 5/15.10(o); $10 for a not-for-profit, 805 ILCS 105/115.10(m); $100 for a limited partnership, 805 ILCS 215/1302(b)(6)) are not modelled.
  * LLCs with series or the ability to establish a series pay $400 instead of $150 (§ 50-10(b)(1)); not modelled in the fee step.
